sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 24.2% a year from $1.70 billion in FY2016 to $12.0 billion in FY2025 [F196][F1][F10].
The shape is a step change rather than a smooth ramp: growth ran 46.2% in FY2017 and 49.1% in FY2020, then slowed to 8.9% in FY2025 [D41][D194][D446].
The FY2020 step came from the U.S. launch of TRIKAFTA in the fourth quarter of 2019 and KAFTRIO in the EU in the third quarter of 2020 [P51].
FY2024 broke the trend with a $232.9 million operating loss [F24], as total acquired in-process R&D of $4.6 billion included $4.4 billion for the Alpine acquisition [P11].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO is the franchise: it was 85.9% of FY2025 revenue [D529] and contributed 13.1pp of the 11.7% growth in FY2024 [D528][D402].
In FY2025 its growth stalled at 0.7%, contributing just 0.7pp, while ALYFTREK added 7.6pp on $837.8 million of first-year sales [D530][D531][D590][S69].
Net product revenues rose $950.5 million, or 9%, in FY2025, which the filing attributes to continued growth without naming a single product [P3].
Operating costs fell 30.4% while revenue grew 8.9%, so revenue growth exceeded operating-cost growth by 39.3pp, at -30.4% cost growth [D457][D464][D446].
Diluted EPS of $15.32 in FY2025 [F75] rose against $3.95 billion of net income [F45] with the diluted share count flat at 258.0 million [X137][D459].
The FY2025 operating margin of 34.8% [F35] sits above the 31.8% window median but below the 48.2% FY2022 high [D663][D662].
The 36.9pp margin recovery in FY2025 [D452] came mostly from the 37.7pp other-lines residual [D468], with SG&A a 1.3pp drag [D467] and R&D a 0.4pp help [D466].
Cost of sales held at 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 as a result of a lower overall royalty rate for the CF medicines [P4][D425].
In FY2025 net margin of 32.9% sat 1.8pp below the 34.8% operating margin [F55][F35][D708], with a 14.9% effective tax rate [D433] and $7.7 million of other expense [X125].
Operating cash flow of $3.63 billion in FY2025 [F85] was primarily due to income from operations of $4.2 billion [P1].
That is 0.92x net income, below the 1.16x window median [D434][D698], and free cash flow of $3.19 billion was 0.81x net income against a 1.11x peer median [F105][D435][D694].
Free cash flow margin was 26.6% [D431], below the 32.8% window median [D669], with capex at 3.6% of revenue and 2.09x D&A [D430][D436].
Stock-based compensation was 18.9% of operating cash flow [D437], and days inventory outstanding rose to 373 days from 287 [D444][D397].
Net cash of $12.3 billion [D439] equals 102.7% of revenue, in the 88th percentile of eight biopharma peers against a -50.7% peer median [D440][D691][D692].
Cash and investments rose to $12.3 billion from $11.2 billion primarily due to increased cash and marketable securities due to product revenue [P2][D438][D392].
Buybacks of $2.02 billion were 63.2% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D441][D442], yet the diluted share count was unchanged at 258.0 million [X137][D459].
The current ratio of 2.90x [F185] is below the 3.52x window median [D678], and return on average equity of 22.5% [D445] trails the 38.7% peer median [D696].
Days inventory outstanding rose 85 days in FY2025 to 373 days [R1][D444][D397], a third consecutive year of increase from 214 days in FY2023 [D350].
Inventory is growing far faster than the 8.9% revenue growth [D446], which ties up cash and raises write-down risk if demand for older CF products keeps shifting.
The effective tax rate moved -300.7pp in FY2025 to 14.9% from 315.5% [R2][D433][D390], a swing the FY2024 filing attributes to non-deductible AIPR&D from Alpine [P5].
The FY2024 rate was a one-off distortion rather than a recurring tax problem, so this flag is benign.
FY2019 share repurchases were later reported as $186.0 million against $192.0 million first reported; the pack uses the first-reported value [R3][X141].
The gap between the two reported figures is immaterial to any conclusion here, but it is a data-quality caveat on that year's capital-return figures [R3][X141].
Whether TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO growth recovers above the 0.7% of FY2025 [D530], or ALYFTREK's 7.6pp contribution [D590] carries the top line, in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether days inventory outstanding falls back below the 287 days of FY2024 [D397] from 373 days [D444] in the FY2026 10-K.
Whether the operating margin holds above the 31.8% window median [D663] from 34.8% [F35] once the FY2025 other-lines residual of 37.7pp [D468] is absent.
